standard_text: The physics of fluids: density, buoyancy and Archimedes' principle; pressure in liquids and gases; Pascal's principle and hydraulic systems; applications in daily life. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, General Science, Term 1)

key_sub: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth.
body_html:
How to think about it

A fluid is a substance that can flow: a liquid or a gas. Density = mass ÷ volume; objects less dense than water float. The upward buoyant force on an object equals the weight of the fluid it pushes aside (Archimedes' principle), which is why steel ships float.

Pressure = force ÷ area. In a liquid, pressure increases with depth, so dams are thicker at the bottom. Pascal's principle: pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is passed on equally in all directions, which is how hydraulic jacks and brakes work.

Example

A 200 g block has a volume of 250 cm³. Will it float?

Density = 0.8 g/cm³

Answer: yes, it is less dense than water

Example

Why are dam walls thicker at the bottom?

Pressure and depth

Answer: the water pressure is greatest at the bottom

Common mistakes

  • Thinking heavy objects always sink.
  • Thinking pressure acts only downward.
  • Mixing up density and mass.

items.q: An object has a mass of 60 g and a volume of 20 cm³. What is its density?
items.e: Density = mass ÷ volume = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 g/cm³. In water (1 g/cm³) it sinks.

items.q: An object has a mass of 96 g and a volume of 80 cm³. What is its density?
items.e: Density = mass ÷ volume = 96 ÷ 80 = 1.2 g/cm³. In water (1 g/cm³) it sinks.

items.q: A steel ship floats, but a steel bolt sinks. Why?
c: The ship's hollow shape displaces a lot of water, so its overall density is less than water.
Steel floats when it is cold.

items.q: Why are oil spills especially harmful to sea birds?
c: Oil makes birds heavier than air only.
Oil coats feathers so they lose buoyancy and warmth.

items.q: Does a steel ship float or sink in water?

items.q: What did Archimedes discover?

items.q: An ice cube has a density of 0.92 g/cm³. Corn syrup has a density of 1.38 g/cm³. What happens when an ice cube is placed in corn syrup?

items.q: What is upthrust?

items.q: What happens to the viscosity of narra syrup when it is warmed?

items.q: Why does a sealed bag of chips puff up at a high altitude?
c: The air pressure outside is lower, so the air inside pushes the bag out.

items.q: How does a hydraulic car lift raise a heavy car with a small force?
